title: Hot-Brewed Loose-Leaf Tea: Black, Green and Oolong
summary: Fresh leaves brewed with precise water temperature and timing to release the full flavour of black, green, or oolong tea.

ingredients.item: loose-leaf black, green or oolong tea (about 1 tsp)
whole milk, for black tea only (optional)

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Heat fresh water to the right temperature for your tea: black tea to 95–100 °C (just boiled), oolong to 85–90 °C, green tea to 70–80 °C (let boiled water stand 3–5 min or add a splash of cold water).

steps.title: Warm
steps.text: Warm the teapot or mug and tip the water out.

steps.title: Add
steps.text: Add about 2.5 g (1 tsp) leaves per 240 ml.

steps.title: Steep
steps.text: Pour over the water and steep for the correct time: black 4–5 min, oolong 5–6 min, green 2–3 min; taste a minute early as overlong steeping or too-hot water makes green tea bitter.

steps.title: Strain
steps.text: Strain or lift out the infuser.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Add whole milk to black tea if liked; oolong and good green leaves can be steeped a second time, a little longer.

tips: Green tea is especially sensitive to temperature; cooler water and shorter steeping time prevent bitterness.
Whole milk works best with black tea; oolong and green tea are traditionally drunk without milk.
safety: Caffeine per 240 ml: black roughly 40–50 mg, oolong roughly 35–40 mg, green roughly 25–30 mg.
storage: Brew and serve fresh. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
